title: Longjing: Dragon Well
description: A micro-lesson that makes Longjing: Dragon Well usable.

hook.text: Longjing (Dragon Well) from Hangzhou is China's most famous green tea, treasured for over 1,200 years.

buildup.text: Flat, sword-shaped leaves are hand-pressed in a hot wok. The technique takes years to master.

discovery.text: Premium Longjing tastes of roasted chestnuts, fresh grass, and a lingering sweetness without any bitterness.

twist.text: The best Longjing—pre-Qingming harvest—is picked before April 5th. After that date, prices drop sharply.

climax.text: Top-grade Longjing can cost over $3,000 per kilogram. It is historically gifted to visiting heads of state.

punchline.text: Flat leaves, hot wok, centuries of craft. That's Dragon Well.

quiz.question: Why is pre-Qingming Longjing more valuable?
options: Picked before April 5th when leaves are youngest and finest

details.summary: Longjing, or Dragon Well, is China's most famous green tea, hand-pressed flat in a hot wok to create its signature chestnut-sweet, toasty flavor. Authentic Longjing comes from Hangzhou's West Lake region, and pre-Qingming harvests in early spring command the highest prices.
details.whyItMatters: Longjing exemplifies how terroir, timing, and artisan processing combine to create a tea considered a national treasure. It has been prized since the Qing dynasty.
takeaways: Longjing is China's most celebrated green tea
Leaves are hand-pressed flat in a hot wok during firing
Pre-Qingming spring harvest is the most prized grade

faq.question: What does pre-Qingming mean for tea?
faq.answer: Qingming is a Chinese solar term falling around April 5th. Tea harvested before this date, called mingqian tea, is the earliest spring pick with the most concentrated flavors. Prices can be ten times higher than later harvests because yields are tiny and demand is enormous.

faq.question: How can you tell authentic Longjing from imitations?
faq.answer: True West Lake Longjing has a protected origin designation. Genuine leaves are flat, smooth, and pale green with a chestnut aroma. The taste is sweet and clean without grassiness. Price is a rough guide too: authentic premium Longjing costs hundreds of dollars per hundred grams.
